content.en:
Planet formation begins in the rotating accretion disk surrounding a newly born star. The Solar Nebular Disk Model (SNDM) is the modern scientific consensus explaining this process.

Solar Nebula Collapse
  • Nebula: A giant interstellar cloud of gas (mostly hydrogen/helium) and microscopic dust collapses under its own gravity.
  • Conservation of Angular Momentum: As the cloud shrinks, it spins faster, flattening into a rotating protoplanetary disk with a protostar at the center.
Thermal Gradient & Frost Line
  • Inner Disk: Hot; only metals and rocky silicates (high condensation temperatures) can solidify.
  • The Frost Line: Located at c. 3-5 AU. Beyond this line, temperatures drop below ~150K, allowing water, methane, and ammonia to freeze into solid ice particles. This boundary dictates planet composition.

The Solar Nebula & Frost Line Boundary:

Thermal Gradient & Planetary Split

content.en:
Planetary growth is a hierarchical accretion process occurring in three distinct phases:

  1. Dust Coagulation (Dust to Planetesimals): Microscopic dust grains collide gently within the disk, sticking together via electrostatic (Van der Waals) forces. They grow into pebbles and eventually kilometer-sized bodies called planetesimals.
  2. Runaway & Oligarchic Growth (Planetesimals to Protoplanets): Once planetesimals exceed ~1 km in size, gravity becomes the dominant force. The largest planetesimals attract smaller ones at a runaway pace, growing into Moon-to-Mars-sized protoplanets.
  3. Clearing the Disk (Protoplanets to Planets): Protoplanets slowly sweep their orbital paths clean of remaining gas and debris through collisions and gravitational ejections, establishing final planetary orbits.

content.en:
The chemical divide of our solar system is a direct consequence of distance from the Sun and the thermal conditions of the nebula disk.

Attribute Terrestrial Planets (Inner) Jovian Planets (Outer)
Primary Composition Rocky silicates, iron, nickel cores. Gases (H, He), water ice, ammonia, methane.
Density & Size High density, small diameters. Low density, massive diameters.
Atmosphere Thin, secondary atmospheres (from volcanic outgassing). Thick, primary atmospheres (captured directly from nebula).
Moons & Rings Few or no moons; no ring systems. Numerous moons; extensive ring systems.

practiceQuestions.q: Who proposed the Nebular Hypothesis of the origin of the Earth in 1796?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Nebular Hypothesis was proposed by Pierre-Simon Laplace in 1796 as a revision of Immanuel Kant's earlier ideas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is the primary difference between Kant's and Laplace's origin hypotheses?
opts: Kant started with a hot rotating nebula, while Laplace assumed cold motionless matter.
Kant started with cold motionless matter, while Laplace assumed a hot, already rotating nebula.
Kant proposed a passing star, while Laplace assumed a binary system.
Kant believed in accretion, while Laplace believed in tidal capture.
practiceQuestions.sol: Kant proposed that a cold, static cloud of dust collapsed and began rotating. Laplace revised this by starting with an already hot, rotating nebula that shed rings as it cooled and contracted.

practiceQuestions.q: The Chamberlin-Moulton Planetesimal Hypothesis (1905) attributes the origin of planets to:
opts: Rings shed by a cooling sun
Filaments of gas pulled from the Sun by a passing star that cooled into solid planetesimals
A giant supernova explosion in a binary companion star
The steady accumulation of interstellar dust in a dark nebula
practiceQuestions.sol: The Planetesimal Hypothesis proposed that a passing star caused explosive eruptions on the Sun, ejecting solar gases that cooled into solid planetesimals, which later accreted into planets.

practiceQuestions.q: The Jeans-Jeffreys Tidal Hypothesis (1919) explains the size distribution of the planets (small at the ends, large in the middle) by proposing:
opts: A cigar-shaped gas filament (tidal filament) pulled from the Sun by a passing star
The collision of two giant gaseous nebulae
The selective stripping of atmospheres by solar winds
practiceQuestions.sol: The Tidal Hypothesis states that a passing star pulled a cigar-shaped filament from the Sun. The thickest part in the center condensed into giant planets like Jupiter and Saturn, while the thinner ends formed smaller planets.

practiceQuestions.q: The Revised Nebular Hypothesis, which introduced friction and collision as the drivers of planet formation within a solar nebula, was proposed by:
practiceQuestions.sol: Otto Schmidt (Russia) and Carl Weizsacker (Germany) revised the Nebular Hypothesis in the mid-20th century by detailing the role of dust-gas friction, collisions, and accretion in a solar nebula disk.

practiceQuestions.q: The boundary in the protoplanetary disk beyond which volatile elements like water, methane, and ammonia freeze into solids is called the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Frost Line (typically located between 3 to 5 AU from the Sun) is the thermal boundary beyond which volatile compounds freeze, enabling the formation of massive icy cores for Jovian planets.

practiceQuestions.q: Why do Terrestrial planets have high densities compared to Jovian planets?
opts: They formed beyond the frost line where heavy gases frozen into ice collapsed under gravity.
They formed in the hot inner disk where only heavy metals and silicates could condense.
They were struck by giant asteroids that compressed their material.
Solar radiation transformed their gases into dense metallic rocks.
practiceQuestions.sol: Terrestrial planets formed close to the Sun where temperatures were too high for volatiles to condense. Only elements with high melting points (metals and silicates) could solidify, leading to a high density.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following processes describes how microscopic dust grains first stick together in the solar nebula to form pebbles?
opts: Electrostatic (Van der Waals) forces during low-velocity collisions
practiceQuestions.sol: Initial dust growth occurs when microscopic grains collide gently and stick together via electrostatic (Van der Waals) forces, a process called coagulation.

practiceQuestions.q: What is a 'planetesimal' in the context of planet formation?
opts: A gas cloud fragment that fails to form a star
A kilometer-sized solid body formed during the early stages of accretion
A moon that has been pulled out of its orbit
A rocky planet that has lost its atmosphere
practiceQuestions.sol: Planetesimals are solid objects, roughly 1 to 100 km in diameter, formed from the accretion of dust grains. They serve as the building blocks of protoplanets.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Planetesimals grow into protoplanets primarily through gravitational attraction.
2. Protoplanets are Moon-to-Mars-sized planetary embryos.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Once planetesimals reach kilometer scale, gravity dominates, driving runaway accretion into protoplanets (planetary embryos).

practiceQuestions.q: The process by which a molten protoplanet separates into layers of differing density (core, mantle, crust) is called:
practiceQuestions.sol: Planetary differentiation is the density-driven separation process where heavy metals (iron, nickel) sink to form the core, while lighter silicates float to form the mantle and crust.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are Jovian planets much larger than Terrestrial planets?
opts: They formed close to the Sun where gas was denser.
They formed beyond the frost line where abundant water ice and gases could be captured by massive solid cores.
They are made of antimatter which expands in space.
They were formed by the merger of multiple stars.
practiceQuestions.sol: Beyond the frost line, solid ice was abundant, allowing protoplanetary cores to grow rapidly to ~10 solar masses. At this threshold, their gravity was strong enough to capture hydrogen and helium gas directly from the nebula.

practiceQuestions.q: What cleared the remaining gas and dust envelope from the solar system, bringing an end to the main phase of planet formation?
opts: Intense solar winds and radiation pressure during the Sun's T Tauri phase
Supernova shockwaves from the Galactic center
The expansion of the Kuiper belt
practiceQuestions.sol: During the T Tauri phase of the young Sun, intense stellar winds and radiation pressure swept the remaining gas and dust out of the solar system, halting gas accretion.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a Jovian planet?
practiceQuestions.sol: Saturn is a Jovian planet (gas giant). Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are Terrestrial (rocky) planets.

practiceQuestions.q: The primary atmosphere of Jovian planets is dominated by which two gases?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jovian planets captured gas directly from the solar nebula, which consisted mostly of hydrogen and helium.

practiceQuestions.q: Why do Terrestrial planets lack thick, primary hydrogen and helium atmospheres?
opts: Their surface temperatures were too cold to retain gas.
Their low gravity combined with intense solar winds stripped away the light gases.
They never accumulated any gas during formation.
The gases dissolved into their molten iron cores.
practiceQuestions.sol: The combination of the inner planets' weak gravity and the young Sun's high temperatures and intense solar wind stripped away the light hydrogen and helium gases.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'secondary atmospheres' of terrestrial planets like Earth and Venus were primarily generated by:
opts: Direct capture from the solar nebula
practiceQuestions.sol: After the primary hydrogen/helium was stripped, terrestrial planets formed secondary atmospheres through volcanic outgassing (releasing CO2, water vapor, nitrogen) and volatile delivery from comets.

practiceQuestions.q: At what temperature does water vapor begin to condense into solid ice in a low-pressure solar nebula, defining the frost line?
practiceQuestions.sol: In the low pressure of the solar nebula, water vapor condenses into ice at about 150 Kelvin (-120°C), which marks the location of the frost line.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nebular Hypothesis:
1. The model assumes a giant cloud of gas and dust collapsed due to gravity.
2. The flat disk shape was a result of the conservation of angular momentum as the nebula contracted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Gravitational collapse initiated the shrink, and conservation of angular momentum caused the rotating cloud to flatten into a disk.

practiceQuestions.q: Which theory of the origin of the Earth is also known as the 'Filament Theory'?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Jeans-Jeffreys Tidal Hypothesis is also called the Tidal/Filament Theory because it centers on a cigar-shaped filament of gas being pulled out from the Sun.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the correct chronological order of the developmental stages of a planet?
practiceQuestions.sol: The accretion sequence is: dust grains coagulating into planetesimals (km-scale), planetesimals merging into protoplanets (embryos), and protoplanets sweeping orbits to form planets.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following compounds condensed as solids beyond the frost line, but remained gaseous in the inner solar system?
practiceQuestions.sol: Water, methane, and ammonia are volatile substances that condensed into solid ice grains only in the cold outer disk beyond the frost line.

practiceQuestions.q: The concept of 'runaway accretion' in planetesimal growth is driven by which physical factor?
opts: The increasing gravitational pull of the largest bodies as they gain mass
Stellar wind pressure pushing rocks together
practiceQuestions.sol: Runaway accretion occurs because gravity depends on mass. As a planetesimal grows larger, its gravity increases, allowing it to sweep up surrounding matter at an accelerating rate.

practiceQuestions.q: The modern consensus model for the formation of the Solar System is known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Solar Nebular Disk Model (SNDM) is the standard model explaining the formation of the Sun and planets from a rotating disk of gas and dust.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following planets has the highest density in the Solar System?
practiceQuestions.sol: Earth has the highest average density (5.5 g/cm³) in the Solar System, followed by Mercury and Venus.

practiceQuestions.q: During planetary differentiation, which element primarily sank to the center of terrestrial planets?
practiceQuestions.sol: Due to its high density and abundance, molten iron (along with nickel) sank to the center of protoplanets, forming metallic cores.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following zones in a protoplanetary disk is characterized by the presence of 'proplyds' (protoplanetary disks) observed today?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Orion Nebula is a famous star-forming region where Hubble has photographed active protoplanetary disks, or 'proplyds', confirming the SNDM theory.

practiceQuestions.q: The hypothesis that the Moon was formed when a Mars-sized body collided with the young Earth is called the:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Giant Impact Hypothesis states that a protoplanet named Theia collided with the early Earth, ejecting debris that accreted to form the Moon.

practiceQuestions.q: What physical parameter determines the transition from 'oligarchic growth' to the final clearing of the planetary disk?
opts: The ignition of hydrogen fusion in the Sun
The cooling of the sun to under 3000 K
The collapse of the Oort cloud
The arrival of a passing binary star
practiceQuestions.sol: The ignition of fusion in the Sun (entering the main sequence) generated the solar wind that cleared the remaining gas disk, halting the growth of gas giants and leaving protoplanets to clear their orbits through collisions.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is NOT a Jovian planet?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mars is a Terrestrial planet, not a Jovian planet.

practiceQuestions.q: With reference to the nebular hypothesis revised by Otto Schmidt, the solar nebula was believed to contain which materials?
opts: Pure iron and nickel vapor only
practiceQuestions.sol: Schmidt's model proposed that the Sun captured a cloud of interstellar dust and gas consisting of hydrogen, helium, and dust particles.

practiceQuestions.q: The Roche Limit is a distance related to planet formation that defines:
opts: The temperature at which silicates melt
The distance within which a celestial body, held together only by its own gravity, will disintegrate due to tidal forces
The outer boundary of the solar system
The distance at which planetary orbits become perfectly circular
practiceQuestions.sol: The Roche Limit is the minimum distance to which a satellite can approach its primary body without being torn apart by tidal forces. Inside this limit, materials cannot coalesce into a moon.

practiceQuestions.q: Which solar system planet has a density lower than that of water, meaning it would float in a giant ocean?
practiceQuestions.sol: Saturn has the lowest average density (0.69 g/cm³) in the Solar System, which is lower than the density of water (1.0 g/cm³).

practiceQuestions.q: The dense metallic cores of rocky planets are surrounded by a layer of silicate rocks called the:
practiceQuestions.sol: In a differentiated planet, the mantle is the thick layer of silicate rock surrounding the dense metallic core.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kant's gaseous hypothesis violated the law of conservation of angular momentum.
2. Kant assumed that collisions between particles could increase the total angular momentum of the system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Kant assumed that random collisions could initiate rotation in a static cloud, which violates the conservation of angular momentum (external torque is needed).

practiceQuestions.q: Laplace resolved the angular momentum problem of Kant's hypothesis by:
opts: Assuming the nebula was already rotating and hot from the start
Proposing that solar wind drove the rotation
practiceQuestions.sol: Laplace assumed the nebula was a hot, rotating mass of gas from the beginning, bypassing the problem of how rotation started.

practiceQuestions.q: In Jeans-Jeffreys Tidal Hypothesis, what happened to the passing star after pulling the filament from the sun?
opts: It went along its path and receded into space
It became a planet of the solar system
practiceQuestions.sol: The passing star continued along its path and moved away. The gravitational pull ceased, leaving the filament in the Sun's vicinity to condense into planets.

practiceQuestions.q: The planetesimals in the early solar system grew by sweep-up. What is this sweep-up mechanism called?
practiceQuestions.sol: Accretion is the process where solid bodies collide and stick together, growing progressively larger.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are terrestrial planets also called 'inner planets'?
opts: They are located inside the asteroid belt, closer to the Sun.
Their atmosphere is trapped inside their crust.
practiceQuestions.sol: Terrestrial planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) lie closer to the Sun, inside the main asteroid belt, and are therefore called inner planets.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following compounds represents the dominant silicate mineral group in Earth's mantle?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Earth's mantle is composed primarily of iron- and magnesium-rich silicates, dominated by olivine and pyroxene.

practiceQuestions.q: Which planet is known as Earth's twin due to its similar size and mass, even though its atmosphere is vastly different?
practiceQuestions.sol: Venus is often called Earth's twin because of its similar size, mass, and density, though it has a runaway greenhouse effect and high surface pressure.

practiceQuestions.q: The gas accretion phase of planet formation must occur quickly (within ~10 million years) because:
opts: Planets fall into the sun if they do not gain mass.
The gas disk dissipates quickly as it is blown away by the young star's stellar winds.
Magnetic fields freeze the gas into solid rock.
practiceQuestions.sol: Protoplanetary disks lose their gas content within 3 to 10 million years due to stellar wind dispersal and accretion onto the central star.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following parts of a differentiated planet contains the lowest density rocks?
practiceQuestions.sol: The crust contains the lightest, lowest-density materials (such as granites and basalts) that floated to the surface during differentiation.

practiceQuestions.q: In the modern model, what triggers the initial collapse of a giant molecular cloud to start star and planet formation?
opts: The expansion of a nearby black hole
An external disturbance such as a supernova shockwave
The heating of the cosmic microwave background
practiceQuestions.sol: External disturbances, such as shockwaves from nearby supernova explosions, compress molecular gas clouds, triggering gravitational collapse.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following solar system bodies are considered primordial leftovers of the planetesimal accretion phase?
practiceQuestions.sol: Asteroids (rocky leftovers in the inner solar system) and comets (icy leftovers in the outer solar system) are primordial planetesimals that were never accreted into major planets.

practiceQuestions.q: What term describes the disk of gas and dust rotating around a protostar before planets are formed?
practiceQuestions.sol: A protoplanetary disk is a rotating circumstellar disk of dense gas and dust surrounding a young newly formed star.

practiceQuestions.q: The division of the solar system into rocky inner planets and gaseous outer planets is primarily determined by:
opts: The temperature gradient of the protoplanetary disk
The spin speed of the Sun
The alignment of the magnetic poles
practiceQuestions.sol: The temperature gradient (hot near the Sun, cold further away) determined which compounds could condense as solids, establishing the terrestrial-jovian divide.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of Jovian planets?
opts: Presence of ring systems and numerous moons
practiceQuestions.sol: Jovian planets have fast rotation rates, ring systems, numerous satellites, and gaseous compositions without solid surfaces.

practiceQuestions.q: The theory that planets formed from a series of concentric rings shed by a shrinking solar nebula is associated with:
practiceQuestions.sol: Laplace's nebular hypothesis centers on the idea that the shrinking, rotating solar nebula shed concentric rings of gas that condensed into planets.

practiceQuestions.q: The Late Heavy Bombardment (LHB) was a phase in solar system history characterized by:
opts: A high rate of asteroid impacts on the inner planets c. 4.1 to 3.8 billion years ago
The collision that created the asteroid belt
The ejection of Pluto from the planet list
practiceQuestions.sol: The LHB was a period approx. 4 billion years ago when a large number of planetesimals were gravitationally perturbed (likely by the migration of outer planets) and bombarded the inner solar system, leaving craters on the Moon and terrestrial planets.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding planetary formation theories:
1. The Nebular Hypothesis of Laplace assumed that the solar nebula was cold and static from the beginning.
2. The Tidal Hypothesis of Jeans-Jeffreys proposed a passing star pulling a filament of matter from the Sun.
3. The Revised Nebular Hypothesis of Schmidt and Weizsacker introduced the role of dust-gas friction and accretion in a disk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect because Laplace assumed the nebula was hot and rotating from the start (Kant assumed it was cold and static).

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the classification of planets in the Solar System, consider the following statements:
1. Terrestrial planets are made of high-melting-point materials because they formed inside the frost line.
2. Jovian planets grew massive cores by accreting abundant water and gas ice beyond the frost line.
3. Jovian planets have thin atmospheres because solar winds are stronger in the outer solar system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because Jovian planets have thick atmospheres due to their high gravity and the fact that solar winds are weaker (not stronger) in the outer solar system, failing to strip their gases.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Arrange the following stages of planetary origin in the correct chronological order:
1. Collitational coagulation of microscopic dust grains via Van der Waals forces.
2. Gravitational runaway accretion of planetesimals into protoplanets.
3. Gravitational collapse of the interstellar molecular gas cloud.
4. Density-driven planetary differentiation into core, mantle, and crust.
Select the correct answer using the codes below:
mockTestQuestions.sol: The correct sequence is: collapse of the cloud (3) -> dust coagulation (1) -> planetesimals to protoplanets (2) -> planetary differentiation (4).

mockTestQuestions.q: Why does Venus possess a dense atmosphere dominated by carbon dioxide, whereas Earth has a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere?
opts: Venus is further from the Sun than Earth.
Venus suffered from a runaway greenhouse effect and lacked liquid oceans to dissolve and lock carbon dioxide into carbonate rocks.
Venus was struck by a carbon-rich giant comet that did not hit Earth.
Earth's gravity is too weak to retain carbon dioxide.
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both Venus and Earth outgassed large amounts of CO2. Earth had liquid oceans where CO2 dissolved and reacted to form carbonate rocks (limestone). Venus, closer to the Sun, lost its water and could not lock up CO2, leading to a runaway greenhouse effect.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the accretion disk of the young Sun:
1. Iron and silicates could solidify throughout the disk, both inside and outside the frost line.
2. Volatile compounds like water ice and methane could only solidify beyond the frost line.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. High-melting-point silicates and metals can solidify anywhere in the disk, but volatile ices can only condense in the cold regions beyond the frost line.

mockTestQuestions.q: With reference to the origin of the Earth, the 'Planetesimal Hypothesis' was proposed by:
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Planetesimal Hypothesis was proposed by Thomas Chamberlin and Forest Moulton in 1905, arguing that planets grew from solid planetesimals pulled out of the Sun.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following is the correct definition of the Roche Limit?
opts: The minimum mass required for a star to trigger hydrogen fusion
The distance within which tidal forces from a primary body will tear apart a satellite held together only by gravity
The boundary distance beyond which gas giants cannot retain hydrogen
The maximum speed at which planetesimals can collide without fragmenting
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Roche Limit defines the boundary within which tidal forces overcome gravitational cohesion, preventing particles from coalescing into a single body or causing moons to disintegrate into rings.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the T Tauri phase of solar evolution:
1. It is a phase of intense solar activity and stellar winds in a young star.
2. The T Tauri solar wind cleared the remaining gas from the protoplanetary disk, halting gas accretion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The T Tauri phase is characterized by strong winds that swept the solar system clean of dust and gas, finalizing planetary masses.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following is the primary evidence supporting the Giant Impact Hypothesis of the Moon's origin?
opts: The Moon's high iron content compared to Earth's mantle
The identical oxygen isotope composition of Earth and Moon rocks, combined with the Moon's lack of a large iron core
The presence of liquid water oceans on the Moon's surface
The fact that the Moon rotates faster than Earth
mockTestQuestions.sol: Moon rocks have the same oxygen isotope ratios as Earth rocks, showing a common origin. Additionally, the Moon has a tiny iron core because it formed from the silicate mantle debris ejected during the impact.

mockTestQuestions.q: What is the role of 'differentiation' in the evolution of Earth?
opts: It created the oceans through chemical reactions.
It caused the density-based layering of Earth into core, mantle, and crust.
It generated the ozone layer by releasing oxygen.
It caused the Earth's orbit to become circular.
mockTestQuestions.sol: Differentiation is the process that structured Earth into a dense metallic core (iron/nickel) and a lighter silicate mantle and crust, driven by gravity acting on a molten early Earth.

en.title: Planetary Accretion Stages
en.decryption: The four main stages: 1. Nebula **C**ollapse into a disk, 2. **P**lanetesimals (dust grains sticking), 3. **P**rotoplanets (gravitational mergers), 4. **D**ifferentiation (dense cores sinking).

en.title: Terrestrial vs. Jovian Atmospheres
en.decryption: Why Jovian planets have thick atmospheres: 1. Weak **S**olar wind at their distance, 2. High **G**ravity from their massive cores, 3. Positioned beyond the **S**now/frost line allowing icy growth.

hi.title: Terrestrial vs. Jovian Atmospheres
hi.decryption: Why Jovian planets have thick atmospheres: 1. Weak **S**olar wind at their distance, 2. High **G**ravity from their massive cores, 3. Positioned beyond the **S**now/frost line allowing icy growth.

fact.en: Trap 1: Atmospheric Loss on Rocky Planets: Rocky (Terrestrial) planets have thin or no hydrogen/helium atmospheres. A common trap is saying this is solely due to low gravity. In reality, it is a combination of low gravity and the intense solar wind of the young Sun, which stripped away light gases in the inner solar system.
fact.hi: Trap 1: Atmospheric Loss on Rocky Planets: Rocky (Terrestrial) planets have thin or no hydrogen/helium atmospheres. A common trap is saying this is solely due to low gravity. In reality, it is a combination of low gravity and the intense solar wind of the young Sun, which stripped away light gases in the inner solar system.

fact.en: Trap 2: Cigar-Shaped Alignment: The Tidal Hypothesis (Jeans-Jeffreys) explains the size distribution of planets (small at the ends, large in the middle like Jupiter/Saturn) as a result of a cigar-shaped gas filament pulled from the Sun. Don't confuse this with the Nebular Hypothesis.
fact.hi: Trap 2: Cigar-Shaped Alignment: The Tidal Hypothesis (Jeans-Jeffreys) explains the size distribution of planets (small at the ends, large in the middle like Jupiter/Saturn) as a result of a cigar-shaped gas filament pulled from the Sun. Don't confuse this with the Nebular Hypothesis.

fact.en: Trap 3: The Frost Line Boundary: Jovian (gas giant) cores grew much larger because they formed beyond the Frost Line (c. 3–5 AU), where water, methane, and ammonia could condense into solid ice grains. Inside the frost line, only rocky silicates and metals could solidify. The frost line is NOT a boundary of temperature alone, but of condensation states.

fact.en: Trap 4: Planetesimals vs. Protoplanets: Planetesimals (kilometer-sized) are formed by electrostatic sticking and collision of dust grains. Protoplanets (Moon-to-Mars-sized) are formed by gravitational accretion of planetesimals. UPSC questions often swap these mechanisms.
